summary: Ship Mountain (old), Del Norte County: a 1914-1922 lookout site with a timber tower, later a trailer; FFLA lists it gone, and a 2008 cab stands about 0.9 km south.

facts.design: Timber tower with a Region 5 Plan 4AR cab (circa 1922), later a portable trailer
facts.status_note: FFLA lists the old site as ground and gone; the trailer was removed in 2007; FFLA lists a two-story cab built 2008 about 0.9 km south on peak 4
facts.agency: US Forest Service, Six Rivers National Forest

events.note: A guard was preparing to take up a station on Ship Mountain (July 1914 item, Siskiyou Bulletin, quoted by Forest Lookouts); the register says a lookout may have been there as early as 1914
Telephone line connecting the Ship Mountain lookout completed June 30, 1915
Timber tower with a Region 5 Plan 4AR cab erected circa 1922 (register); a 1939 forest history says a standard lookout cabin was packed 26 miles in and constructed in 1922
Al Gastman took over the lookout station in August 1922 (Blue Lake Advocate, quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Milton Kingsley to hold the lookout position in June 1924, after two years under Gastman (Blue Lake Advocate, quoted by Forest Lookouts)

September 1924 lightning storm set many fires in the Siskiyou and Klamath forests; one Ship Mountain lookout reported lightning in 2648 places in his territory that night (Spokane Daily Chronicle, quoted by Forest Lookouts)
AWS Station Mike 8-1 placed on inactive status October 17, 1943; AWS had added sleeping quarters to the site
Portable trailer lookout in use at the site since 1973 (FFLA Western Region 2008 report); the register dates the trailer to the 1960s
Portable lookout trailer removed and the road to the summit improved (Forest Lookouts)
New two-story lookout station constructed in 2008 (Forest Lookouts; register); FFLA lists a two-story cab on peak 4, about 0.9 km south-southwest of the old site

corrections.why: The register gives this record's coordinates (41.7356, -123.79298) and says the lookout served as AWS Station Mike 8-1 in World War II; Forest Lookouts gives the same station and inactive date. Medium confidence, since the station is recorded for the peak as a whole.

The register describes a timber tower with a Region 5 Plan 4AR cab (circa 1922), and the 1941 and 1952 survey notes describe a two-story lookout house. 'Ground' reflects only the FFLA's present listing that nothing stands on the old spot. Editor to decide whether to keep the FFLA type.

notes_for_editor: The register page for Four Brothers (US 1313, CA 136) gives coordinates 41.735609, -123.792981, which are exactly this record's coordinates. The FFLA lists the standing two-story cab at 41.72813, -123.79548, about 0.9 km south-southwest, and the datasheet note puts the current house on peak 4. So the register's coordinates may describe the old peak 3 site, while the 2008 cab is on peak 4. The Four Brothers record's coordinates may need checking. The register's 1960s date for the trailer and the FFLA 2008 report's 1973 date conflict; both are in the story. The 1941 and 1952 survey descriptions of a two-story wooden house on peak 3 do not fit neatly with a c. 1922 timber tower unless the two were one structure; unresolved. The sibling story us-ca-ship-mountain-four-brothers covers the same history from the current cab's side and should be kept consistent with this one.
